To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

BDNF‐induced Arc expression requires Ras‐Raf–MAPK signaling through extracellular‐regulated kinase (ERK) and intracellular Ca2+ and calmodulin (Cam) in cultured cortical neurons, and the regulation of Arc transcription is differentially tailored to the complex neuronal activity.
the induction of Arc by BDNF is regulated by Ras‐Raf and ERK, and that [Ca2+], CaM, CaMK, PLC, and PI3K are involved in the regulation of Arc by neuronal activity.
BDNF‐induced Arc upregulation in neurons is mediated through the Ras‐Raff‐MAPK signaling pathway and that Ca2+‐induced Arc transcription involves the PI3K, CAMK, and Ras‐Raff MAPK pathways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel mechanism of BDNF‐induced Arc transcription in cortical neurons.
the role of calcium in neuronal plasticity and the regulation of gene expression by calcium in neurons.
the role of BDNF in synaptic plasticity, and the molecular mechanisms of the BDNF‐regulated immediate early gene Arc in cortical neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Arc transcription can be regulated by multiple signaling pathways in response to different stimuli.
the regulation of Arc transcription in cortical neurons is highly complex and is dependent upon the nature of the stimulus, which is likely to reflect the complex and diverse functions of this gene.
the Ras‐Ras‐MAPK signaling pathway, which is mediated through ERK activation, is a critical component of BDNF‐induced Arc transcription.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BDNF‐induced transcriptional up‐regulation of Arc is mediated by ERK, but is regulated by [Ca2+] i and CaM.
the regulation of Arc transcription is highly dependent on the signaling pathways and their cross‐talks.

BDNF‐ and Ca2+‐induced Arc transcription are mediated by distinct signaling pathways, but both pathways are regulated by the same transcription factor, NF‐κB, and that the Ras‐Ras‐MAPK‐ERK signaling pathway is the major signaling pathway for BDNF‐induced Arc up‐regulations in cultured cortical neurons
The main takeaway from our work is that
BDNF‐induced Arc up‐regulates in a Ca2+ dependent manner, but ERK signaling is not coupled with Ca2+.
Arc transcription is regulated by distinct signaling mechanisms, depending on whether the neuronal activity is induced by Ca2+ or BDNF.
BDNF and neuronal activity regulate Arc transcription through distinct signaling pathways that are tailored to the specific features of the signals.
